question_message:
To tailor what counts as “abroad” and identify realistic AI PhD directions and programs, please provide:
- Your citizenship and current country of study/residence
- Current/highest degree, field, institution type, GPA or class rank, and expected graduation date
- Main AI interests (e.g., machine learning, computer vision, NLP, robotics, AI safety, or interdisciplinary AI)
- Research, publication, internship, and programming experience
- English proficiency/test status and any other language constraints
- Funding needs, budget limits, and preferred or excluded countries
simulator_answer:
- Citizenship is not specified. I currently study and reside in Jiangsu, China.
- I am an undergraduate in Computer Science and Technology at a prestigious university in Jiangsu. My academic performance is excellent, and I have received school scholarships for two consecutive years. My exact GPA/class rank and expected graduation date are not specified.
- My main interests are AI and algorithm research, especially deep learning and natural language processing. I prefer applied, implementation-heavy, system-building work over purely abstract theory.
- I have substantial hands-on programming and self-directed learning experience using PyCharm, VS Code, GitHub, Coursera, and technical resources, and I have participated in programming competitions. Specific formal research projects, publications, internships, and programming languages are not specified.
- My English proficiency, test status, and other language constraints are not specified.
- Strong funding or scholarships and cost-effectiveness are important. No exact budget, preferred countries, or excluded countries are specified.

question_message:
1. Which AI research areas most interest you—or which 2–3 currently attract you if undecided? This will determine the lab shortlist and technical preparation plan.
2. What is your primary intended post-PhD outcome: academia, industrial research, applied R&D/startup, or undecided? This will change how programs are weighted for publications, internships, industry links, and placement.
3. What is your current academic and research-readiness profile (degree/field and expected graduation, grades or standing, math/programming preparation, and research/publications)? This will determine realistic program tiers and the 1–2 year gap-closing plan.
simulator_answer:
1. Deep learning and natural language processing interest me most, especially applied, implementation-heavy work.
2. Industrial research is my primary intended outcome, while keeping strong employability and applied R&D options.
3. I’m an undergraduate in Computer Science and Technology at a prestigious university in Jiangsu. My expected graduation date is not specified. I have excellent academic performance and received school scholarships for two consecutive years, but exact grades/rank are not specified. My preparation is strongest in programming and self-directed, hands-on learning through coding tools, online platforms, technical blogs, GitHub, and programming competitions. My formal math preparation and research/publication record are not specified.

3. Which should dominate the destination choice: easiest travel/accessibility, most dependable July beach weather, best value, calmest swimming, or widest activity mix? This changes the shortlist, ranking, and itinerary emphasis.
